name: Polwarth
headline: One Nation out of contention
meaning: The VEC is counting preferences between Liberal and Labor, but One Nation is ahead of Labor on first preferences. The real contest is likely Liberal against One Nation, and the projection uses that.
One Nation is second on first preferences with 24.9%, behind Liberal on 40.9%.
To win, One Nation needs about 73.4% of the 34.2% of votes that went to other candidates to flow its way ahead of Liberal.
The VEC's preference count is between Liberal and Labor, so it expects One Nation to miss the final two. If One Nation beats one of them on primaries, the VEC will redo the preference count.
The Greens candidate is third on 17.2%. Greens voters overwhelmingly put One Nation last, which hurts it here.
Only about 5.9% of enrolled voters are counted. Early booths are often small and unrepresentative.
